newsitem.title: USA: Ill. Clinton nuclear plant restart still unclear.
newsitem.headline: Ill. Clinton nuclear plant restart still unclear.

text.p: Restart of the 930 megawatt (MW) Clinton nuclear power plant remained unclear as the operator, Illinois Power Co, still faces safety issues raised by the Nuclear Regulatory Commisson (NRC).
The NRC said in its January 2 daily plant status report that Clinton could resume operation as early as January 18.
"It's up to the plant manager," Illinois Power spokesman John Dewey replied when asked about Clinton's restart, adding no date has been set.
The Clinton generating facility was shut Sept 5, 1996, to correct a recirculation pump problem. The outage was extended to address safety issues and to refuel the plant.
"We're finished the refueling outage. It's dependent on whether the workers are ready for restart," Dewey said.
Jan Strasma, an NRC spokesman, called a January 18 restart "a little optimistic," adding the plant is more likely to return to service late this month or early February.
"The concerns were the soft issues: attitudes and philosophy," said Strasma.
NRC was concerned by the way plant workers prepared for Clinton's shutdown to repair recirculation pumps.
"They were handling events leading to the shutdown with less of a focus on safety. They were more intent on keeping the plant running," said Strasma.

Illinois Power officials have been examining four areas of operation at Clinton: conservative decision-making/human performance, procedural compliance, management oversight and plant material conditions.
To correct weaknesses in those areas, the company replaced the plant's manager, revised operating procedures and retrained onsite personnel, Dewey said.

NRC and Illinois Power officials are scheduled to meet later this month over safety issues at Clinton. After the enforcement conference, the regulatory agency would consider whether to fine the company for safety violations. he said.
Illinois Power holds an 86.8 percent stake in Clinton, while Soyland Power Cooperative and Western Illinois Power Cooperative owns the remaining interests.
